scenes.vo_line: Milk is just water, protein, fat, vitamins, and sugar. But cheesemaking transforms it into something totally different.
scenes.visual_direction: b-roll or simple illustration supporting the on-screen text

scenes.vo_line: Enzymes break down the milk—basically mimicking your stomach's digestive process.
scenes.visual_direction: b-roll or simple illustration supporting the on-screen text

scenes.vo_line: The lactose drains away with the whey, while fat, vitamins, and minerals stay with the protein curds.
scenes.visual_direction: b-roll or simple illustration supporting the on-screen text

scenes.vo_line: Then comes the magic: controlled growth of bacteria, molds, and yeast during aging. These microbes are added during processing, rubbed on rinds, or applied through washing liquids.
scenes.visual_direction: b-roll or simple illustration supporting the on-screen text

scenes.vo_line: That bright orange grocery store cheddar? It's colored with annatto from the tropical achiote tree—not naturally orange at all.
scenes.visual_direction: b-roll or simple illustration supporting the on-screen text

scenes.vo_line: Humans have been perfecting this chemistry for thousands of years. What's your favorite cheese?
scenes.visual_direction: b-roll or simple illustration supporting the on-screen text
